subject: Re: Security questionnaire and DPA onboarding — PII scope & transfer clarifications
messages:

Subject: Security questionnaire and DPA onboarding — initial questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to start the security questionnaire (SSQ) and DPA onboarding so we can get procurement and legal aligned. A few items are blocking our internal review and procurement timeline:

1) PII scope: can you confirm what fields you consider PII when customers upload content (examples: full name, email, phone, government IDs, medical data)? We need a short mapping for our DPA annex.
2) Cross-border transfers: do any of your subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, telemetry services) process customer content outside the US? If so, which countries/regions?
3) Tokenization & retention: for customer-provided files containing PII, what tokenization / pseudonymization options do you offer, and can we control retention per-tenant?
4) Evidence: can you provide KMS attestation or SOC-2 artifact references for encryption at rest and export controls?

Attached is our SSQ template (we trimmed it down). Would appreciate a short answer to each item so procurement can move to the SOW/DPA redlines. If it's easier, happy to schedule a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Alice Wells
Security Lead — Onboarding
HealthTech Inc.
[phone: +1-415-555-0198]

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (privacy) and Connor (ops) to provide the detailed responses and evidence. High-level answers below to keep procurement moving:

• PII scope: Redwood treats obvious identifiers (name, email, phone, government IDs) and sensitive categories (health, financial) as PII. We’ll provide a mapping table (CSV) for the annex.
• Cross-border: Core hosted inference runs in regional clusters; subprocessors may operate in US/EU/APAC depending on region. We'll enumerate subprocessors and locations in the next message.
• Tokenization/retention: We offer tenant-configurable retention and tokenization options (redaction on ingest, reversible pseudonymization via customer key).
• Evidence: we can provide KMS attestation extracts and our SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer view.

I’ve attached the initial fills and the dataflow diagram Marissa prepared — please treat the doc as draft while we confirm subprocessors.

Best,

Hi Alice — thanks for sending this over. I expanded Rafael’s notes into concrete answers below (pulled from our privacy playbook). I kept each answer short so your procurement/legal team can paste into the SSQ form; happy to expand any section.

=== PII scope (short mapping) ===
- Identifiers: full name, email address, phone number, postal address, usernames — treated as PII.
- Sensitive identifiers: SSNs, passport numbers, driver’s license — treated as highly sensitive PII; flagged for additional redaction and short retention by default.
- Health & financial: clinical notes, device data, billing numbers — treated as sensitive categories, require customer enablement for processing.
- Unstructured content: customers can mark fields as PII during ingestion; otherwise we rely on configured redaction rules.

=== Cross-border transfers & subprocessors ===
- Core serving infrastructure is operated on regional clusters (US, EU, APAC).
- Subprocessors: our primary cloud provider (us-east & eu-west), telemetry & analytics provider (hosted EU/US), and managed KMS (US primary, EU replica for EU customers). A full subprocessors table (name, purpose, region) is attached.
- We support routing policy to keep EU customer data in EU clusters; this is configurable at onboarding and captured in the DPA annex.

=== Tokenization, pseudonymization & retention ===
- Tokenization: reversible pseudonymization is available via customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key). Tokens are opaque identifiers stored separate from the cleartext blobs if the customer opts in.
- Redaction-on-ingest: we can apply regex/ML redaction pipelines to strip or mask PII before persistent storage.
- Retention: tenant-level retention is configurable (30/90/365/never-delete), with default 90-day telemetry retention and customer-data retention set by contract.

=== Evidence & artifacts ===
- KMS: we can provide KMS configuration screenshots and a dated attestation for key custody procedures; for BYOK we can provide a procedural checklist.
- SOC 2: we can share an NDA-gated excerpt of our SOC 2 Type II report (control mapping for encryption, access control, and change management).
- Dataflow diagram: attached (redwood-dataflow-diagram.vsdx) includes ingress points, tokenization layer, and storage segregation.

Next steps we propose:
1) Rafael — provide the subprocessors table with countries and subprocess roles (I’ve stubbed this in the attachment).
2) Alice/HealthTech — flag any required residency constraints (e.g., EU-only processing) so we can enable routing.
3) Schedule a short call (30 min) if you want walk-throughs of the KMS attestation and dataflow.

Notes: we prefer to capture residency and retention requirements in the DPA annex (Annex A) rather than via hard-coded product settings, unless you need enforcement at the infra layer (in which case we’ll route to our Private offering).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Manager — Redwood Inference

Marissa — this is great, thanks. A few follow-ups from our security team after reviewing your diagram:

1) For customer-uploaded files with mixed PII (documents with names + clinical notes), can Redwood perform tokenization at ingest and ensure the token store never leaves the customer region? If token store replication is needed for HA, can it be restricted to customer-specified regions?
2) If we request EU-only processing, is there a technical gating that prevents inference requests from spilling to non-EU clusters (including telemetry pipelines)? You mentioned routing policy; we need confirmation that telemetry can be kept in-region or pseudonymized before routing out.
3) Evidence: procurement asked for a sample KMS attestation for BYOK workflows and an example redaction pipeline config (regex/ML) — are those available as redacted artifacts?

We are aiming to move to procurement review by next Thursday. If you can reply inline to the three items above and attach the sample artifacts, we’ll flag the DPA annex items to legal. Otherwise, happy to take the 30-min call.

Best,
Alice Wells
Security Lead — Onboarding
HealthTech Inc.
